title: Cutaway
description: A cutaway shot leaves the primary action for a related detail, observer, or part of the same world. It is used for context, reaction, compression, or continuity repair.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: A cutaway is a brief exit: a clock, a kettle, a street, a person listening in a doorway. Its value is the relation it adds, not merely that it hides a bad join.
It can build anticipation, let the room comment, or imply that time has passed. It is the wrong tool when the object is the plot in the actor's hands: that is an insert.
It is also the wrong tool if the return to the main action restarts a gesture that should have continued. Check temporal logic.
A cutaway can be a pressure release; it can also cheat geography if the new view could not exist at that moment.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Choose a detail that can plausibly be present now. Match ambient light and, in editorial thinking, room sound.

Return to the main action at a later phase of the motion, not at the same frame of a handshake. Prompt: Cutaway from [Subject] to a related detail in the same world, a pressure-release or information beat that is not an insert on the actor.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it to hide a cut, show a clock, or let the room comment: a kettle trembling during an argument, a courtyard while someone looks. Do not cut away to a new geography that implies false time, and do not call an object-in-hand a cutaway.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: An Insert Shot stays on a plot object inside the action. A Reaction Shot is a person's response, often a face; a cutaway might be that listener, or it might be a non-human detail.
A cut-in goes tighter on something already in the master, same space and often same axis, without leaving the beat. Cutaway means you left.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Hot Fuzz uses cutaways as both joke and glue. The Conversation lets the world around a listener comment.
Dancer in the Dark brackets a car conversation with wider and closer views. Jurassic Park punctuates approaching threat with environmental details and observers.
Grammar: leave, add a relation, return honestly.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Name the exit. Example: Cutaway from [Subject] to a related detail in the same world (a clock, a kettle, a street, a listener), not an insert on the actor.
Match the key. For video, hold the detail, then imply a return; do not keep the original action in frame if you meant to leave it.

A couple argues quietly in a kitchen. Cut away to a kettle beginning to tremble on the stove while their voices continue, then return to the couple after a tense pause. Generate the insert separately with matching light and room sound. No literal symbolism captions.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is an Insert Shot (object in the action) or a random pretty detail. The tell is a letter in the hero's hands labeled cutaway, or a return that rewinds the action.
Fix: leave the primary beat, pick a plausible now, watch time on the way back.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Cutaway in film?
A cutaway is a shot away from the primary action, used for context, reaction, compression, or continuity repair. It might be a clock, a street, an observer, or a piece of the room.
Cutaway vs Insert Shot

An insert is a close view of a story object or hand fact inside the action. A cutaway leaves that action for a related view. Hands on the plot letter are an insert; the kettle on the stove during the fight is a cutaway.
When should I use Cutaway?
Use it to add a relation, hide a join, compress time, or let the world comment. Do not use it to show the object in the actor's hands, and do not return in a way that rewinds the action.
How do I prompt Cutaway for AI image or video?
Write Cutaway from [Subject] to a related detail in the same world, and name that detail. Say it is not an insert on the actor. Match light to the main scene.
